messages:
alex: FYI — Acme's security questionnaire follow-up arrived. They want clarifications on RBAC changes, audit log retention, and KMS integration for Private deployment. Need short answers by EOD.

maria: can you paste the specific questions?

alex: excerpt: "Please describe how role changes are reviewed and enforced, what audit logs are retained (user actions, model invocations), retention periods, and whether customer-managed KMS keys can be used with Private. Also: key rotation, export controls, and access revocation process."

kevin: TL;DR answers we can give: 1) RBAC changes go through PR + security review + automated policy checks, 2) Audit logs include admin API calls, deployment events, token usage metadata (no full model outputs), retention configurable up to 7 years, default 90 days, 3) Private supports customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS), key rotation supported, HSM recommended for high-reg.

maria: important to be precise about what we log. customers often assume we log full prompts. we must say clearly we do not store PII by default and model payload retention is configurable.

jordan: agree. proposed language: "We retain structured audit events (actor, action, resource, timestamp, request metadata). Full request/response payloads are not retained unless explicitly enabled by the customer for debugging and are subject to DLP review."

alex: good. also need the RBAC enforcement flow. kevin can you draft snippet?

kevin: paste below (config example):
```yaml
rbac:
  roles:
    - name: infra_admin
      permissions: [deploy:create, model:rollout, secrets:read]
    - name: reader
      permissions: [model:invoke, logs:read]
  change_review: 
    required_approvals: 2
    approvals_from: [security_team, infra_team]
  enforcement: policy_agent (OPA) + admission webhook
```

maria: add a line about automated tests: policy CI runs on PRs and flags privilege escalation.

kevin: updated snippet in my draft answer.

alex: KMS details: Acme asks if they can use their own key and whether encryption in transit/at-rest uses that key. Answer: yes for Private — customer-managed keys for data at rest; we integrate with their cloud KMS via IAM roles. We do envelope encryption: service generates DEK, DEK encrypted by customer KMS. Key rotation handled by KMS — we support re-encrypting DEKs on rotation.

jordan: do we need to mention BYOK constraints for on-prem? e.g., HSM-only?

kevin: for on-prem we support HSM or local KMS appliance; people typically choose HSM for FIPS workloads. note: offline key export is prevented by default.

maria: audit retention values — they want explicit numbers. our recommended defaults: 90 days retention for interactive logs; 365 days for admin/change logs; archival up to 7 years on request (cost pass-through). Must state we can export to customer S3/GCS bucket for long-term retention.

alex: add incident response and access revocation: If a key compromise occurs, revocation steps: 1) revoke key in KMS, 2) rotate DEKs and re-encrypt where possible, 3) deprovision affected service principals, 4) notify customer and run IR runbook.

jordan: include a short paragraph on evidence we can provide for their auditor: KMS rotation logs, CloudTrail/Stackdriver entries, and RBAC change PR history + signed approvals.

maria: I'll stitch this into a one-page response. quick ask: can someone confirm we don't keep model outputs in analytics pipelines?

kevin: confirmed — analytics pipelines only store aggregated metrics (latency, token counts, error rates). we do not persist raw outputs unless customer opts-in and signs data handling agreement.

security-bot: "Reminder: CISO review call scheduled Thu 11:00 UTC with Acme. Meeting link: https://meet.company/secure-call"

alex: thanks. maria — please send draft to me + kevin by 15:00 so we can review before CISO call. I'll own the call notes and deliverable. :thumbsup:

maria: on it, uploading draft in a minute.

kevin: ping me if you need a one-liner on technical integration.

alex: awesome. closing loop when sent.
